subject: Unexpected 429s impacting Acorn Health - routing review & evidence delivery

Subject: Unexpected 429s across tenant — need logs + immediate next steps

Hi Naomi,

We started seeing a spike of HTTP 429s for our production integration around 08:40 PT this morning. The errors are affecting the submit endpoint and causing downstream job backpressure. I've attached a screenshot and a short snippet from our error logs (attached).

Can you confirm whether this is on your side (rate limiting policy change, throttling, routing) or if we need to do anything on our end? We need:
- A quick description of what changed on Redwood's side (if anything)
- Any tenant-level log slices you can share for 08:30–09:30 PT
- ETA for a mitigation or rollback if this is a config issue

This is impacting scheduled batch jobs; any ETA you can provide is appreciated.

Thanks,
Lena

Hi Lena — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot. I'm escalating to engineering now and cc'ing Karthik and Grace. Initial notes:

- We see a correlated increase in 429 responses for tenant acorn-prod in our routing logs starting ~08:37 PT.
- No planned deploys or policy changes recorded in the control plane at that time.

Immediate next steps from our side:
1) I'll collect tenant-scoped logs and a short packet of debug traces for 08:30–09:30 PT and share via a secure S3 link in the next hour.
2) Karthik will validate ratecap mappings and routing policies for your tenant ID to check for translation/lookup issues.
3) If this is a misconfiguration, we'll produce a config diff and apply a one-line hotfix with a rollout window.

We will also prepare a formal incident note and a remediation timeline. Apologies for the disruption — we'll treat this as P1 until it stabilizes.

Can you confirm the tenant ID you saw in your logs? (send the tenant id if convenient)

Best,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Lena Morris <lena@acornhealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s across tenant — need logs + immediate next steps

Hi Naomi/Lena — quick technical update and root cause context.

Summary:
- Root cause: a routing-key translation regression introduced by a recent autoscaler refactor. The translation table that maps external tenant tokens to internal ratecap buckets had a missing fallback rule for tenants with hyphenated IDs (e.g., acorn-prod). When the lookup failed, requests were routed to a fallback bucket with a much lower quota, resulting in unexpected 429s.
- Time window: 08:37–09:02 PT (we applied the fix at ~09:00 PT).

What we changed:
- Applied a config patch to restore the fallback rule and added an explicit mapping for acorn-prod. Patch: config-diff.patch (attached).
- Replayed queued requests where safe — we have a partial replay log.
- Added a short-term mitigation: increased the fallback bucket quota for affected nodes so clients wouldn't hit 429s during reconfiguration.

Artifacts we've generated and how to access them:
- Tenant-scoped debug logs (08:30–09:30 PT): s3://redwood-incident-logs/acorn/2027-06-20/ (linked above).
- Raw server traces and KV lookup failures: redwood-ratecap-debug.log (attached).
- Control plane change diff: config-diff.patch (attached).

Credits and next steps:
- We're preparing a billing reconciliation and credit for any rejected calls during the incident window. Nail-shaped estimate pending (we'll provide a formal credit amount after log reconciliation).
- We'll run a post-deploy verification for hyphenated tenant IDs across canary and prod tomorrow morning.

If you want the raw logs in another format (CSV, zipped archive), say the word and we'll deliver. Also happy to hop on a quick call if you want walk-through.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
SRE Lead, Inference Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-ratecap-debug.log (text/plain), config-diff.patch (text/plain)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Morris <lena@acornhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 429s across tenant — closure, credit offer, and follow-up actions

Hi Lena — following up with a concise post-incident summary and next steps.

1) Root cause: as Karthik described, a regression in the routing-key translation logic caused hyphenated tenant IDs to miss their intended ratecap bucket, routing them into a low-quota fallback.
2) Mitigation applied: explicit mapping for acorn-prod restored and fallback bucket quota raised at 09:00 PT on 2027-06-20. No follow-on 429s observed after 09:02 PT.
3) Artifacts delivered:
   - Logs: s3://redwood-incident-logs/acorn/2027-06-20/ (contains per-request traces and KV lookup failures)
   - Debug dump: redwood-ratecap-debug.log (attached)
   - Config diff: config-diff.patch (attached)

4) Compensation: We will reconcile rejected requests and propose a credit amount against your June invoice. Expect a reconciliation email by Friday (2027-06-25) with line-item details.

5) Preventative actions (short/medium term):
   - Short: add guardrail validation for translation-table entries and an automated canary that verifies hyphenated and underscore tenant IDs in staging. (ETA: 72 hours)
   - Medium: extend the routing test suite and add a runtime alert when fallback-bucket utilization exceeds 30% of quota for any customer. (ETA: 14 days)

6) Optional: we can provide a signed evidence packet (control-plane audit log extract) and an exec summary for your SOC/audit team. If you want that, we'll deliver via a secure DocuSign/S3 package and include a formal incident timeline.

If acceptable, please confirm you received the logs and whether you want the invoice credit reconciliation or a call to review the artifacts.

Apologies again for the disruption — we're treating this as high-priority and will share the postmortem when complete.

Best regards,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
